correctness.rationale: The frozen RESULT.md proof is sound: in K_r (r≥3) all proper vertex subsets and no full vertex set admit a common neighbor, hence ∂Δ_C embeds for each maximal clique block. For a cut-vertex union G∪_v H of connected odd-cycle graphs, the exact neighborhood complex is N(G)∪N(H)∪Δ_{A∪D}, with N(G)∩N(H)={v} and attachment intersection Δ_A ⊔ Δ_D; the homotopy pushout adds one 1-cell connecting points in a path-connected complex, hence one S1 and no new higher homology. Pendant K2 blocks collapse via a simplex attached along a nonempty face. Inducting over the block-cut tree yields exactly b−1 extra S1 plus ∂Δ_C≃S^(|C|−2), tree case S0, and the line graph of a tree branch-degree corollary. Relative homology of the disjoint face attachment supports inclusion-induced integral higher Hk basis, and automorphisms give permutation signs on oriented simplex boundaries. Independent finite checks of Betti patterns, gluing face-set identities and an oriented symmetry example passed; these do not prove the infinite result.
residual_risks: No formal Lean/expert verification; the finite mod-two verification cannot establish higher integral homology or all-order homotopy type.
Homotopy equivalence is noncanonical in degree one; no equivariant wedge splitting of H1 is asserted.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge statement-and-implication comparison finds no inspected theorem covering every block graph (arbitrary clique sizes and block-cut attachment shapes) together with canonical oriented clique-boundary high-degree signed action. Crucially, published clique-join formula ALREADY covers star unions of n equal-sized clique blocks, and this partial coverage is explicitly acknowledged rather than misrepresented as novel. A potentially close one-point-union thesis concerns D-neighborhood complexes containing 0 and does not apply to the open-neighborhood D={1}. Kozlov, Matsushita, Braun–Vega and Shukla do not dominate the general claim. Residual risk is a differently named old articulation-vertex decomposition theorem; search failure is not novelty proof.
residual_risks: Historical/unindexed cut-vertex gluing theorem for ordinary open neighborhood complexes could imply all wedge multiplicities; not exhaustively excluded.
The uniform star-of-cliques subfamily is actually covered by an independently published Resultary theorem, so novelty cannot be attributed to that subfamily alone.
An unindexed equivariant high-degree homology statement for clique trees might dominate signed block-permutation modules even if phrased through another complex.

value.rationale: This is a natural complete homotopy classification for the infinite family of finite connected block graphs. The clique sizes alone determine mixed sphere dimensions and multiplicities despite the varied attachment shapes; line graphs of trees furnish a canonical branch-degree application. The oriented clique-boundary classes give usable integral higher homology and the automorphism action, beyond rank counts. This is a motivated all-parameter topological invariant rather than a recomputation of a small table. Strict clique-star subfamily previously covered, but arbitrary block-cut trees and unequal clique dimensions are the remaining motivating scope.
residual_risks: No classification of general chordal graphs with large clique intersections.
First-homology equivariant representation is deliberately not determined.

limitations: Ordinary homotopy rather than canonical simple-homotopy collapse; degree-one splitting not asserted equivariantly.
General connected block graphs only, not arbitrary chordal graphs.
Originality is best of knowledge; a strict star-of-equal-cliques subfamily is covered in existing published work; an unindexed broader gluing theorem remains a live risk.
Pre-existing expert/Lean channels are not performed and cannot be claimed as certified.
